sourceReview:
Attested by the worker. Every function named in the boundary was read in the C source before it was written: zap.c destroyable() (5612-5650), inventory_resistance_check() (5709-5718) with adtyp_to_prop() and u_adtyp_resistance_obj() above it, destroy_strings[][3] (5778-5787), maybe_destroy_item() (5797-5954), destroy_items() (5964-6097) and zhitu()'s ZT_FIRE arm (4421-4439); potion.c potionbreathe() (1931-2118); do.c trycall() (393-400); do_name.c docall() (640-676); attrib.c exercise() (498-518); win/tty/topl.c update_topl() (251-279).

Four things the earlier plan did not settle, each decided against the source rather than the trace. First, potionbreathe()'s fall-through group is nine types, not the seven C's comment at 2096-2105 names: POT_SEE_INVISIBLE and POT_ENLIGHTENMENT have no case label either, and the switch has no `default:`, so they reach the same nothing. scripts/potion.test.mjs asserts that split by parsing potion.c with its block comments separated from its code. Second, objnam.c cxname() is xname(), which pluralises but prints no count, so C's `yname(obj)` for three scrolls reads 'your scrolls of blank paper' and not 'your 3 scrolls'; the message tests were corrected to that reading. Third, the deferred second pass of destroy_items() is not empty for AD_FIRE after all: POT_LEVITATION carries oc_oprop LEVITATION and is a potion, so a wielded one satisfies 6062-6064. The unreachable disjunct is the POT_WATER one at 6066-6068, because js/u_init.js:371 writes NON_PM into u.ulycn and js/eat.js:1363 stops set_ulycn(). Fourth, C's `yname()` reaches shk.c shk_your() and its mon_owns() arm for an object in a monster's pack, which js/shk.js stops at; the monster arm of the message therefore keeps its do_name.c monsterPossessive() construction and says so at the site, while the hero arm calls Yname2() and yname() as C does.

Five mutants survive the slice's own lines and no test can kill any of them. Three are boolean: `let xresist = false` and `skip = true` inside maybe_destroy_item(), and `deferred: false` in destroy_items()'s reservoir initializer. C's own comment calls the first group lint suppression; every reader of xresist is preceded by the AD_FIRE case's assignment, and the other two cases stop above it. The Book of the Dead arm breaks with quan still 0, so with skip false the rn2(3) loop runs zero times, `if (!cnt) return 0` returns the same 0, and nothing observable differs. Every reservoir slot the destroy loop reads was written by the walk, which sets deferred in the same statement as oid and otmp. Two are relational: `limit > MAX_ITEMS_DESTROYED` and `elig_stacks > limit`, both clamps that assign the value they compare against, so `>` and `>=` differ only where the assignment is a no-op.
